main_text.p: m corpori illatam per utrumque du-um in intestinum tenue continuò roruit, ad minorem copiam illorum umorum, qui in statu naturali intestina blandè stillant: quan-quidem eadem est materia, iidem nt humores, eædem & gradibus ntaxat diversæ acrimoniæ, iidem, iamvis magis aut minùs acti, spiri-s & calor excitantes & cooperantes; em denique est locus, in quo inte-inum illud prælium committitur. t certè, perquàm ridiculum foret lle videre effervescentiam illorum umorum, & impedire media, quibus in conspectum prodeat; aut non mittere præternaturalem animalis nstitutionem, & velle scrutari inte-norum contenta.
Misella igitur est argumentatiun-la, quâ triumphum ante victoriam nens pag. 14. ait D. Graefium suo se jugulare gladio, quia videlicet ille ncedit succum panci eaticum foris

page.notes: The left edge of the scan cuts off the first one or two letters of many lines; these are reproduced only where visible. Catchword "cum" and the single letter "E" below the text are as printed. Doubtful: "panci eaticum" may be "pancreaticum" with a printing break; "spiri-s" and "inte-inum" are line-end hyphenations of partly visible words.
